questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a practice problem, what product forms when sodium borohydride reduces 2-butanone?

options.misconception: hydride reduction does not remove oxygen
a ketone does not reduce to an aldehyde

questions.explanation: Sodium borohydride delivers hydride to the carbonyl carbon of 2-butanone, and protonation of the alkoxide gives the secondary alcohol 2-butanol.
questions.hint: Hydride reduction of a ketone gives a secondary alcohol.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: When analyzing the transformation, what class of alcohol results from adding a Grignard reagent to formaldehyde?

options.misconception: an aldehyde other than formaldehyde gives secondary

questions.explanation: Formaldehyde has two hydrogens on the carbonyl carbon, so addition of one carbon group and workup gives a primary alcohol with one carbon substituent.
questions.hint: Formaldehyde gives a primary alcohol.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a tutorial session, which set of conditions converts an aldehyde into an acetal?

options.text: A limited amount of water with base
options.misconception: water drives acetals back to the aldehyde

options.text: An excess of alcohol with acid catalysis

questions.explanation: An aldehyde reacts with excess alcohol under acid catalysis, with water removed, to form an acetal through a hemiacetal intermediate; excess alcohol drives the equilibrium forward.
questions.hint: Excess alcohol and acid give an acetal.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: You are given the following: which reagent converts a ketone into an imine?

options.misconception: a secondary amine gives an enamine
a tertiary amine has no N-H to condense
ammonia gives a primary imine but the general case is a primary amine

questions.explanation: A primary amine condenses with a ketone under acid catalysis with water removal to give an imine, while a secondary amine gives an enamine because it lacks a second N-H for imine formation.
questions.hint: Primary amine means imine; secondary means enamine.

provenance.author: orgchem2-bank-author
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In a synthesis planning session, what kind of reagent converts a ketone into an alkene in the Wittig reaction?
questions.explanation: A phosphorus ylide, such as a triphenylphosphonium carbanion, reacts with a ketone to give an alkene and triphenylphosphine oxide, placing the double bond exactly at the former carbonyl carbon.
questions.hint: The Wittig reagent is a phosphorus ylide.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: A laboratory report asks: which group migrates preferentially in the Baeyer-Villiger oxidation of an unsymmetrical ketone?

options.misconception: migratory aptitude is electronic, not just steric
that is not the controlling factor

options.text: The group that best stabilizes positive charge

questions.explanation: In the Baeyer-Villiger oxidation the group with greater migratory aptitude, roughly tertiary greater than secondary greater than primary greater than methyl, migrates to oxygen because the transition state has carbocation character.
questions.hint: The more substituted carbon migrates better.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For this reaction scenario, what functional group forms when hydrogen cyanide adds to an aldehyde?

options.text: A cyanohydrin with a new C-C bond

questions.explanation: Addition of cyanide to an aldehyde forms a cyanohydrin bearing both a hydroxyl and a nitrile on the former carbonyl carbon, creating a new carbon-carbon bond in a nucleophilic addition.
questions.hint: Cyanide adds to give a cyanohydrin.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In the laboratory (example), why are aldehydes generally more reactive than ketones toward nucleophilic addition?

options.text: Aldehydes have less steric hindrance and less alkyl donation

options.misconception: aldehydes have at most one alkyl group

options.text: Ketones have a more electrophilic carbon
Ketones lack a carbonyl pi bond
options.misconception: both have a carbonyl pi bond

questions.explanation: Aldehydes are more reactive because they bear at most one electron-donating alkyl group and less steric bulk at the carbonyl, making the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic and more accessible.
questions.hint: Less donation and less crowding means faster addition.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: In your notebook, answer: which reagent reduces an aldehyde to a primary alcohol but leaves an ester intact?

options.misconception: that would also reduce the ester
that can reduce esters under forcing conditions

questions.explanation: Sodium borohydride is a mild hydride donor that readily reduces aldehydes and ketones but generally leaves esters untouched, whereas lithium aluminum hydride is much more powerful.
questions.hint: Sodium borohydride is mild and selective.

questions.stem: A mechanistic quiz asks: why are aldehydes generally more reactive than ketones toward nucleophilic addition?

Aldehydes have less steric hindrance and less alkyl donation

questions.explanation: Aldehydes are more reactive because they bear at most one electron-donating alkyl group and less steric bulk at the carbonyl, making the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic and more accessible.
questions.hint: Less donation and less crowding means faster addition.

questions.stem: A chemist observes the following: what functional group forms when hydrogen cyanide adds to an aldehyde?

options.text: A cyanohydrin with a new C-C bond

questions.explanation: Addition of cyanide to an aldehyde forms a cyanohydrin bearing both a hydroxyl and a nitrile on the former carbonyl carbon, creating a new carbon-carbon bond in a nucleophilic addition.
questions.hint: Cyanide adds to give a cyanohydrin.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: A quiz question asks: why are aldehydes generally more reactive than ketones toward nucleophilic addition?

options.misconception: aldehydes have at most one alkyl group

options.text: Ketones have a more electrophilic carbon
Aldehydes have less steric hindrance and less alkyl donation
Ketones lack a carbonyl pi bond
options.misconception: both have a carbonyl pi bond

questions.explanation: Aldehydes are more reactive because they bear at most one electron-donating alkyl group and less steric bulk at the carbonyl, making the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic and more accessible.
questions.hint: Less donation and less crowding means faster addition.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: For the sample reaction, which reagent reduces an aldehyde to a primary alcohol but leaves an ester intact?

options.misconception: that would also reduce the ester
that can reduce esters under forcing conditions

questions.explanation: Sodium borohydride is a mild hydride donor that readily reduces aldehydes and ketones but generally leaves esters untouched, whereas lithium aluminum hydride is much more powerful.
questions.hint: Sodium borohydride is mild and selective.

questions.subject: ORGANIC_CHEMISTRY_II
questions.stem: During a lab exercise, which amine reacts with cyclohexanone to form an enamine?

options.text: A secondary amine such as pyrrolidine

options.misconception: a primary amine gives an imine

questions.explanation: A secondary amine condenses with a ketone by loss of water to give an enamine, in which the nitrogen is attached to a carbon that is double bonded to the alpha carbon of the original ketone.
questions.hint: Secondary amines form enamines.
